1.1 Define \(S(\theta)=\sum_i\min(\lambda_i,\theta)\) for \(0\le\theta\le\max_i\lambda_i\). It is continuous, \(S(0)=0\), and \(S(\max_i\lambda_i)=\sum_i\lambda_i\). If \(0\le\theta_1<\theta_2<\max_i\lambda_i\), some \(\lambda_j>\theta_2\), so the \(j\)-th summand increases strictly and the others do not decrease. Thus for \(0<D<\sum_i\lambda_i\), the intermediate-value theorem gives a unique \(\theta\) with \(S(\theta)=D\). [given, algebra]

1.2 For \(t>0\), \(\ln t\le t-1\): if \(t\ge1\), integrate \(1/u\le1\) on \([1,t]\); if \(0<t<1\), use \(\ln t=-\int_t^1du/u\) and \(1/u\ge1\) on \([t,1]\). Hence \(-\ln t+t-1\ge0\). [given, algebra]

1.3 Fix \(0<D<\sum_i\lambda_i\), its \(\theta\), and \(c=(2\theta\ln2)^{-1}\). If \(\lambda_i>\theta\), then for \(0<\delta_i\le\lambda_i\),
$$\phi_i(\delta_i)-\phi_i(\theta)+c(\delta_i-\theta)=\frac{-\ln(\delta_i/\theta)+\delta_i/\theta-1}{2\ln2}\ge0$$
by step 1.2; the inequality also holds at \(\delta_i=0\) because \(\phi_i(0)=+\infty\). If \(0<\lambda_i\le\theta\), then \(\phi_i(\lambda_i)=0\), and for \(0<\delta_i\le\lambda_i\), step 1.2 gives
$$\phi_i(\delta_i)\ge\frac{1-\delta_i/\lambda_i}{2\ln2}\ge\frac{\lambda_i-\delta_i}{2\theta\ln2}=-c(\delta_i-\lambda_i).$$
It holds at \(\delta_i=0\) by the infinite-value convention. A zero eigenvalue has only \(\delta_i=0\) and contributes zero. Thus for every feasible coordinate, \(\phi_i(\delta_i)\ge\phi_i(\delta_i^*)-c(\delta_i-\delta_i^*)\), with \(\delta_i^*=\min(\lambda_i,\theta)\). [given, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Summing the supporting inequalities in step 1.3 and using \(\sum_i\delta_i\le D=\sum_i\delta_i^*\) proves \(\sum_i\phi_i(\delta_i)\ge\sum_i\phi_i(\delta_i^*)\). The latter sum is exactly \(\frac12\sum_i\log_2^+(\lambda_i/\theta)\); the allocation is feasible, so it attains the minimum. [given, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 If \(D=0\), nonnegativity forces every \(\delta_i=0\), giving the two stated cases. If \(D\ge\sum_i\lambda_i\), choose \(\delta_i=\lambda_i\) for every i; all rates are zero, and no feasible objective can be negative. These cases complete the endpoint and degenerate branches. [given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎"

      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** Nonempty finite alphabets \(\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}\), a source pmf \(p\), and finite nonnegative distortion \(d\).

[F1] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]: for a finite joint pmf, mutual information in nats is its finite joint-law KL sum.

[F2] [[thm-it-information-unit-conversion]]: mutual information in bits is the finite nats value divided by \(\ln2\).

[F3] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]: closed bounded subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space are compact.

[F4] [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]: a continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact metric space attains a minimum.



1.1 For each \(x\), choose a minimizing \(\hat x_x\) from the nonempty finite set \(\widehat{\mathcal X}\); finite choice is available by successive selection from finitely many nonempty sets. The deterministic channel \(W(\hat x\mid x)=\mathbf1_{\{\hat x=\hat x_x\}}\) has expected distortion \(D_{\min}\). Conversely, each channel row is a probability vector, so its conditional mean distortion is at least \(\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)\); averaging against \(p\) shows every channel has distortion at least \(D_{\min}\). Thus feasibility is equivalent to \(D\ge D_{\min}\). [given, algebra]

1.2 For a probability vector \(q\), set \(H(q)=-\sum_i q_i\ln q_i\), with \(0\ln0:=0\). The scalar function \(-t\ln t\) on \((0,1]\) extends continuously to zero because \(\lim_{t\downarrow0}t\ln t=0\); hence entropy is continuous on every finite simplex. Expanding the finite KL sum in [F1] gives \(I(X;\widehat X)=H(p)+H(q)-H(p_{X\widehat X})\), where \(q(\hat x)=\sum_xp(x)W(\hat x\mid x)\); all terms are continuous functions of the channel coordinates. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Identify all channels with a point in \([0,1]^{|\mathcal X||\widehat{\mathcal X}|}\). The row-sum equalities, nonnegativity inequalities and expected-distortion inequality define a closed set; the cube makes it bounded. When feasible it is nonempty, so [F3] makes it compact. [F3, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 By [F2], division by the positive constant \(\ln2\) preserves continuity. Thus the bit mutual-information objective is continuous on the nonempty compact feasible set in step 2.1; [F4] gives a point where it attains its minimum. This proves attainment. [F2, F4, step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎"

      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A finite source pmf, finite nonempty reproduction alphabet, and finite nonnegative distortion.

[F1] [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]]: \(R(D)\) minimizes finite mutual information over channels meeting the mean-distortion constraint and is \(+\infty\) when infeasible.

[F2] [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]: feasibility is equivalent to \(D\ge D_{\min}\), and every feasible minimum is attained on a finite channel simplex.

[F3] [[lem-it-finite-log-sum-inequality]]: the finite log-sum inequality applies to nonnegative finite arrays, with zero terms interpreted by continuity.

[F4] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]: mutual information is the finite joint-KL sum; it is finite for finite alphabets.

[F5] [[thm-it-finite-kl-nonnegative-equality]]: finite KL divergence is nonnegative.

[F6] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]: closed bounded subsets of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space are compact.



1.1 Feasibility at every \(D\ge D_{\min}\) and attainment are given by [F2], so \(R(D)\) is finite there; [F5] gives \(R(D)\ge0\). If \(D_2\ge D_1\), every channel feasible at \(D_1\) is feasible at \(D_2\), so the infimum cannot increase. [F1, F2, F5, given]

1.2 Fix \(D_0,D_1\ge D_{\min}\), \(t\in[0,1]\), and channels \(W_0,W_1\) feasible at those budgets. Set \(W=tW_0+(1-t)W_1\); its distortion is at most \(tD_0+(1-t)D_1\). For each \((x,\hat x)\), apply [F3] to the two joint-mass terms \(t p(x)W_0(\hat x|x),(1-t)p(x)W_1(\hat x|x)\) and corresponding product-marginal terms \(t p(x)q_0(\hat x),(1-t)p(x)q_1(\hat x)\), then sum over \((x,\hat x)\). The resulting inequality is \(I_W(X;\hat X)\le tI_{W_0}(X;\hat X)+(1-t)I_{W_1}(X;\hat X)\), in nats and therefore also in bits. [F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 The constant channel outputting a minimizer of \(\mathbb E d(X,\hat x)\) has distortion \(D_{\rm c}\) and zero mutual information. For \(D\ge D_{\rm c}\), this channel is feasible, so [F5] gives \(R(D)=0\). [F1, F5, step 1.1, given]

2.2 Choose minimizing channels at \(D_0,D_1\) by [F2] and use their mixture from step 1.2. The mixture is feasible at \(tD_0+(1-t)D_1\) and has rate at most \(tR(D_0)+(1-t)R(D_1)\); taking the infimum proves convexity. [F1, F2, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 Fix feasible \(D\) and any sequence \(D_k\downarrow D\). The values \(R(D_k)\) increase to a finite limit \(L\le R(D)\) by step 1.1. Choose a minimizing channel \(W_k\) at each \(D_k\). The finite channel simplex is a closed bounded subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space, hence compact by [F6]; a subsequence converges to a channel \(W_\infty\). Distortion is a finite linear function of channel entries, hence \(W_\infty\) is feasible at \(D\). Mutual information is continuous on the finite channel simplex by the entropy formula and continuity of \(-u\ln u\) at zero, so along this subsequence \(I(W_k)\to I(W_\infty)\ge R(D)\). Since the same subsequence of values converges to \(L\), we obtain \(L\ge R(D)\), proving right-continuity. [F1, F2, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Steps 1.1–3.1 prove every assertion, including the degenerate case \(D_{\rm c}=D_{\min}\), where the constant channel already gives zero on the entire feasible interval. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3] ∎"

      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A Bernoulli source parameter \(p\in[0,1]\), binary reproduction, and Hamming distortion.

[F1] [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]]: \(R(D)\) is the minimum finite mutual information in bits over test channels of expected distortion at most \(D\).

[F2] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]: finite mutual information is the finite joint-law KL sum, with base-2 values in bits.

[F3] [[thm-it-finite-conditional-mutual-information-identities-and-equality]]: conditional mutual information is a finite conditional KL sum and is nonnegative.

[F4] [[thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule]]: finite conditional entropy obeys the chain rule.

[F5] [[thm-it-finite-kl-nonnegative-equality]]: finite mutual information and conditional mutual information are nonnegative.



**Given:** The objects in the statement and suppliers [F1]–[F5].

1.1 Let \(Y\) be any test-channel output and put \(E=X\oplus Y\), where \(\oplus\) is addition modulo two; write \(e=\mathbb P(E=1)=\mathbb E d(X,Y)\). Since \(X=Y\oplus E\), the map \((Y,E)\mapsto X\) is deterministic and bijective in E for each Y, so \(H(X|Y)=H(E|Y)\). By [F4], \(H(E)-H(E|Y)=I(E;Y)\), and this mutual information is nonnegative by [F3] and [F5]; hence \(H(E|Y)\le H(E)=h_2(e)\). If \(0\le D\le p_0\le1/2\) and \(e\le D\), then \(h_2(e)\le h_2(D)\): on \((0,1/2)\), \(h_2'(u)=\log_2((1-u)/u)\ge0\), and continuity supplies the endpoints. The entropy identity in [F4] therefore gives \(I(X;Y)\ge h_2(p)-h_2(D)\). [F2, F3, F4, F5, given, algebra]

1.2 Suppose \(0\le D\le p_0\) and \((p,D)\ne(1/2,1/2)\). Then \(1-2D>0\) and \(q:=(p-D)/(1-2D)\in[0,1]\): nonnegativity follows from \(D\le p\) (since \(D\le p_0\)), while \(q\le1\) is equivalent to \(p+D\le1\), which follows from \(D\le1-p\). Let \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), independently let \(E\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(D)\), and set \(X=Y\oplus E\). Then \(\mathbb P(X=1)=q(1-D)+(1-q)D=D+q(1-2D)=p\), and the Hamming distortion is exactly \(D\). [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 If \(D\ge p_0\), reconstructing constantly by the more probable source symbol has expected Hamming distortion \(p_0\) and zero mutual information; [F5] makes zero the minimum. This proves the formula on that branch, including deterministic sources. [F1, F5, step 1.1, given]

3.1 Since E is independent of Y and determines X given Y, \(H(X|Y)=H(E|Y)=H(E)=h_2(D)\). Thus \(I(X;Y)=h_2(p)-h_2(D)\), attaining the converse in step 1.1. The excluded corner \(p=1/2,D=1/2\) is covered by step 2.1. This proves the formula for all parameters. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, given, algebra] ∎"

      "item_id": "lem-it-stationary-block-rdf-limit-and-endpoint-continuity",
      "status": "repair",
      "strategy": "direct",
      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A stationary process on a finite nonempty source alphabet, a finite nonempty reproduction alphabet, and bounded finite nonnegative distortion.

[F1] [[def-it-stationary-finite-block-information-rdf]]: \(nR_n(D)\) is the minimum block mutual information in bits subject to normalized additive distortion; \(D_{\min}\) is the pointwise minimum mean distortion and \(D_{\rm c}\) is the best constant-reproduction distortion.

[F2] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]] and [[thm-it-information-unit-conversion]]: finite mutual information is a finite KL sum and bits equal nats divided by \(\ln2\).

[F3] [[lem-finite-block-entropy-chain-rule]] and [[thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule]]: finite entropy is subadditive and the chain rule holds.

[F4] [[lem-it-finite-log-sum-inequality]]: finite log-sum gives convexity of mutual information in a channel for fixed input law.

[F5] [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]: every feasible finite block channel minimum is attained.

[F6] [[thm-it-finite-markov-data-processing]]: finite information cannot increase under deterministic postprocessing.



1.1 Write \(a_n(D)=nR_n(D)\), and choose minimizing channels for blocks of lengths \(m\) and \(n\), available by [F5]. Use their conditional product as a channel on the concatenated block. Stationarity gives the same marginal laws for the second block as for a block of length \(n\); each part has mean distortion at most \(D\), so the concatenated normalized distortion is at most \(D\). [F1, F5, given, construct]

1.2 A best constant reconstruction has normalized expected distortion \(D_{\rm c}\) and zero mutual information for every block; nonnegativity of finite KL gives \(R_n(D)=0\) for \(D\ge D_{\rm c}\). If \(D<D_{\min}\), every coordinate distortion is at least its pointwise minimum, so no block channel is feasible and each \(R_n(D)=+\infty\). [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.3 Suppose \(D_{\rm c}>D_{\min}\), and let \(\gamma\) be the smallest positive value among the finite gaps \(d(x,\hat x)-\min_zd(x,z)\); thus \(\gamma>0\). Fix \(0<\epsilon<\gamma/2\). Since \(D_{\min}+\epsilon\) is feasible, [F5] supplies a minimizing length-\(n\) channel at that distortion budget. Let \(S_i=1\) when its chosen reproduction has positive gap from the pointwise minimum, and let \(\alpha=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb P(S_i=1)\). The excess above the block minimum is at least \(\gamma\sum_i S_i/n\), so \(\alpha\le\epsilon/\gamma\). [F1, F5, given, algebra]

1.4 Keep the selected channel's original reproduction at coordinates with \(S_i=0\), and replace coordinates with \(S_i=1\) by a pointwise minimizing symbol for the observed source letter; call the resulting reproduction \(\widehat X'^n\). Its distortion is exactly \(D_{\min}\) coordinatewise. The original output, flags, and correction symbols determine \(\widehat X'^n\), so [F6] and the chain rule/entropy bounds give

2.1 Let \((X_1,Y_1)\) and \((X_2,Y_2)\) denote the two source/output block pairs under that channel. Conditional independence of the two channel outputs given the full source block gives \(H(Y_1,Y_2\mid X_1,X_2)=H(Y_1\mid X_1)+H(Y_2\mid X_2)\). Entropy subadditivity gives \(H(Y_1,Y_2)\le H(Y_1)+H(Y_2)\). Subtracting these finite quantities and using [F3] yields \(I(X_1,X_2;Y_1,Y_2)\le I(X_1;Y_1)+I(X_2;Y_2)\), so \(a_{m+n}(D)\le a_m(D)+a_n(D)\). The source blocks need not be independent. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix \(k\ge1\), write \(n=qk+r\) with \(0\le r<k\), and put \(a_0=0\). Repeated subadditivity gives \(a_n\le qa_k+a_r\). The finite set \(\{a_r:0\le r<k\}\) is bounded, so \(\limsup_n a_n/n\le a_k/k\). Taking the infimum over \(k\), while \(\inf_k a_k/k\le\liminf_n a_n/n\), proves \(a_n/n\to\inf_k a_k/k\). [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For each fixed \(n\), the feasible block-channel sets are nested as \(D\) increases, so \(R_n(D)\) is nonincreasing. Mixing two block channels and applying [F4] shows \(R_n\) is convex. Passing to the pointwise limit from step 3.1 preserves both monotonicity and the convexity inequality. [F1, F4, step 3.1]
\[
I(X^n;\widehat X'^n)\le I(X^n;\widehat X^n)+H(S^n)+\sum_i\mathbb P(S_i=1)\log_2|\widehat{\mathcal X}|.
\]
By entropy subadditivity and concavity of binary entropy, \(H(S^n)\le n h_2(\alpha)\). Thus \(R_n(D_{\min})\le R_n(D_{\min}+\epsilon)+h_2(\epsilon/\gamma)+(\epsilon/\gamma)\log_2|\widehat{\mathcal X}|\), since \(h_2\) is increasing on \([0,1/2]\). [F1, F3, F6, step 1.3, algebra, construct]

5.1 Taking infima over \(n\) in step 1.4 gives the same inequality for \(R_{\rm block}\). The two error terms tend to zero as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\); monotonicity from step 4.1 gives the reverse bound \(R_{\rm block}(D_{\min}+\epsilon)\le R_{\rm block}(D_{\min})\), proving right-continuity. If \(D_{\rm c}=D_{\min}\), step 1.2 already gives zero on the entire feasible interval. [step 4.1, step 1.2, step 1.4, algebra] ∎"

      "file": "items/thm-it-finite-alphabet-rate-distortion-coding-theorem.md",

      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** An iid finite-alphabet source, finite reproduction alphabet, bounded finite nonnegative distortion, and budget \(D\ge0\).

[F1] [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]]: \(R(D)\) is the minimum test-channel mutual information in bits, with infeasible value \(+\infty\).

[F2] [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]]: operational rates use deterministic fixed-length codes; the expected criterion has limiting expected distortion at most \(D\), and the excess criterion requires every positive slack.

[F3] [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]: feasible finite test-channel minima are attained exactly for \(D\ge D_{\min}\).

[F4] [[lem-it-rate-distortion-convexity-and-monotonicity]]: \(R\) is nonincreasing and right-continuous throughout its feasible domain.

[F5] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]] and [[thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule]]: finite mutual information equals \(H(X)-H(X|Y)\), and conditional entropy obeys the chain rule.

[F6] [[thm-it-finite-markov-data-processing]]: finite mutual information cannot increase along a Markov chain.

[F7] [[thm-it-finite-conditional-mutual-information-identities-and-equality]]: finite conditional mutual information is nonnegative, so conditioning cannot increase entropy.

[F8] [[cor-iid-finite-variance-weak-law]]: averages of iid square-integrable real variables converge in probability to their common mean.



**Given:** The source, alphabets, distortion and budget, together with suppliers [F1]–[F8].

1.1 Let a deterministic length-\(n\) code have \(M_n\) messages and reconstruction \(\widehat X^n\). Data processing [F6] gives \(I(X^n;\widehat X^n)\le H(f_n(X^n))\le\log_2M_n\). Put \(D_n=\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\), and let \(T\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), independent of all variables; set \((X,Y)=(X_T,\widehat X_T)\). Since the source symbols are iid, \(H(X^n)=\sum_iH(X_i)\). By [F5], the chain rule, and conditioning reducing entropy from [F7],
\[
I(X^n;\widehat X^n)=\sum_i\bigl[H(X_i)-H(X_i\mid X^{i-1},\widehat X^n)\bigr]\ge\sum_i I(X_i;\widehat X_i).
\]
Also \(I(X;Y\mid T)=n^{-1}\sum_iI(X_i;\widehat X_i)\), while \(I(X;T)=0\); the chain rule and nonnegative conditional information [F7] imply \(I(X;Y)\le I(X;Y,T)=I(X;Y\mid T)\). Thus \(R(D_n)\le I(X;Y)\le n^{-1}I(X^n;\widehat X^n)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n\), since \(\mathbb E d(X,Y)=D_n\). [F1, F5, F6, F7, given, algebra]

1.2 Assume \(D\ge D_{\min}\), and choose a minimizing test channel \(W(\hat x|x)\) by [F3]. Let \(Y\) have its induced output pmf, and let \((X_i,Y_i)\) be iid copies of the test-channel pair. Its information density \(\imath(X;Y)=\log_2[W(Y|X)/P_Y(Y)]\), on positive joint support, is finite-valued because the alphabets are finite; it has mean \(I:=R(D)\). The block distortion is bounded with mean at most \(D\). The iid law of large numbers therefore gives, for every \(\eta,\delta>0\),

2.1 For an expected-distortion code sequence with \(\limsup_nD_n\le D\), eventually \(D_n\le D+\epsilon\), so step 1.1 and monotonicity give \(R(D+\epsilon)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n\). For an excess-distortion sequence and any \(\epsilon>0\), boundedness gives \(D_n\le D+\epsilon+d_{\max}\mathbb P(d_n>D+\epsilon)\), hence eventually \(D_n\le D+2\epsilon\); then \(R(D+2\epsilon)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n\). Taking limsups and using [F4] as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves both operational rates are at least \(R(D)\) whenever feasible. If \(D<D_{\min}\), every reconstruction has block distortion at least \(n^{-1}\sum_i\min_{\hat x}d(X_i,\hat x)\); its mean is \(D_{\min}\), and the iid law of large numbers makes it converge in probability to \(D_{\min}\). Thus neither operational criterion is feasible below \(D_{\min}\). [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, given, algebra]
\[
\mathbb P\{d_n(X^n,Y^n)\le D+\eta,\ \sum_{i<n}\imath(X_i;Y_i)\le n(I+\delta)\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The distortion and information-density summands are bounded on finite alphabets, hence square-integrable; [F8] applied to each iid sequence proves both convergences in probability and the displayed joint event. [F1, F3, F8, given, algebra]

2.2 For each source word \(x^n\), let \(G_n(x^n)\) be the reproduction words satisfying both inequalities in step 1.2. The joint probability of this event tends to one, so the source probability of the set where \(P(Y^n\in G_n(X^n)\mid X^n)<1/2\) is at most twice the probability of the complement and tends to zero. On the other source words, every \(y^n\in G_n(x^n)\) satisfies \(P(y^n|x^n)/P_Y^n(y^n)\le2^{n(I+\delta)}\); summing this likelihood-ratio inequality over the good set yields \(P_Y^n(G_n(x^n))\ge\frac12 2^{-n(I+\delta)}\). [F1, step 1.2, given, algebra]
